computer-science/big-o.md: An algorithm that is fast on your test data can stall on real input. Learn to read growth rates and upper bounds, and when constant factors still decide.
computer-science/arrays-and-strings.md: Contiguous memory makes indexing cheap and insertion costly. Learn the patterns, two pointers, sliding windows and prefix sums, that turn quadratic scans into linear ones.
computer-science/linked-lists-stacks-que: Some problems need order, not random access. Learn when linked structures, stacks and queues fit, and the pointer techniques interviews keep returning to.
computer-science/hashing.md: Constant-time lookup is a promise with conditions. Learn how hash tables work, what collisions and resizing cost, and how hashing collapses search problems.
computer-science/trees.md: Hierarchies and ordered data both become trees. Learn traversals, binary search trees and the recursive reasoning most tree problems need.
computer-science/graphs.md: Dependencies, networks and grids are graphs in disguise. Learn representations, breadth- and depth-first search and the shortest-path and ordering patterns built on them.
computer-science/heaps-and-priority-queu: Sometimes you only need the next most important item. Learn how heaps keep that cheap and where top-k and scheduling problems use them.
computer-science/sorting-and-searching.m: Order is often the cheapest structure to add. Learn the sorting trade-offs and binary search on values as well as on positions.
Some problems are easiest to state as smaller copies of themselves. Learn recursion, its stack cost and backtracking through choices with pruning.
computer-science/dynamic-programming.md: Brute force that repeats work can often remember it instead. Learn to spot overlapping subproblems, define state and build answers bottom-up.
computer-science/greedy-and-intervals.md: A locally best choice is sometimes globally right. Learn when greedy choices are provably safe, and the interval patterns built on sorting.
computer-science/system-complexity.md: Data-structure choices reappear as production behaviour. Reconnect algorithmic cost to memory, latency and scale in real systems.
computer-science.md: Data structures and algorithms in the order interviews and production code use them: structures first, then the algorithms that operate on them, then their cost in real systems.
